text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.2% today to $367.19, extending a sharp two-week decline of 1.5%. The drop reflects the broader weakness in refining margins over the past week: US crude oil prices fell from $95+ per barrel earlier this month to $89.53 today, while refineries are running at 95.7% capacity with gasoline and diesel inventories elevated. When oil prices drop faster than refining demand can absorb the supply, margins compress and profitability pressure hits refiners directly.

The geopolitical risk story that boosted oil prices earlier this month—the Iran conflict threatening the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane—has not prevented the recent selloff, suggesting markets may be pricing in either supply resilience or a shift away from immediate crisis concerns. With data center electricity demand expected to surge and energy infrastructure getting renewed permitting attention, the refining sector is caught between near-term margin headwinds and longer-term structural questions about fuel demand.
